messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) water’s freezing point is slightly below its normal 0 °C.  
According to the water phase diagram, the melting line has a negative slope, so the freezing point drops as pressure falls. At 10 kPa the freezing point is roughly **–2 °C** (about –3.6 °F).  

So, water would freeze at about –2 °C when the ambient pressure is 10 kPa.
